rv.q: There is no doubt it is a compelling production, if not exactly an enjoyable one.
Whether all these musical elements come together to form an entirely convincing whole is another question, but there's no denying the composer's imagination or her willingness to push boundaries.
It’s impressively executed with all the panache, commitment, and technical excellence that we have come to expect from ENO, but overall is somehow rather disappointing.
Williams’ bold production is a technical marvel, but it’s hard to imagine anyone but the greatest theatrophiles connecting to this story in its current form.

cn.t: Critics find this Pulitzer-winning opera on human trafficking heavy-handed and unengaging, with an overwhelming multimedia production that fails to connect despite its poignant subject matter.
